seo.title: Swarm Protocol: defend the page from a bug swarm
seo.description: Bugs eat a real webpage's letters into binary and drain its buttons. Squash the swarm in this free browser defense game: click or tap, no install.

sections.heading: Swarm Protocol
sections.body: Release a swarm onto this page, then defend it. Bugs eat letters into binary, grow stronger and drain your buttons. Squash them before the interface falls apart. It plays right here in your browser: no install, and Recall gives the page back.

spans.text: Play it here, then make it part of your own project. Visit GitHub for the source code, setup instructions, and integration examples.

image.alt: Swarm Protocol in play on its own DOM VIRUS page: bugs crawl over the heading, eaten letters turn into 0s and 1s and the scoreboard tracks button integrity

items.title: Release the swarm
items.body: Press Play. The bugs arrive in your viewport, near the pointer.

items.title: Squash the bugs
items.body: Click or tap a bug to squash it. Bugs that have eaten grow stronger and can take more than one hit.

items.title: Save the buttons
items.body: Bugs eat letters into 0 and 1, grow, and hunt the page's buttons. Squash them before the buttons lose their colour.

items.title: Rescue distant attacks
items.body: When bugs attack a button off screen, an edge alert offers Jump from 50 points or Jump + Zap from 200. Scrolling there yourself is always free.

items.title: Recall the page
items.body: Press Escape or Recall to end the round and restore the page.

items.title: Scroll to outrun them
items.body: Scrolling can outrun the swarm, and it never costs points.

items.title: Rescues get pricier
items.body: Every rescue raises the Jump and Zap prices by 25 points, and each zap adds another 150. Prices reset on restart.

items.title: Zaps don't pay
items.body: A zap clears a 140–220 px radius around the destination but returns only 1 point per kill, with no combo multiplier.

items.title: The secret code
items.body: On sites that install the hidden activation, ↑ ↑ ↓ ↓ ← → ← → B A Enter opens the game.

items.title: Squash crawlers before six letters
items.body: A crawler has one hit point. After six letters it grows and gains a hit point, and after twelve it becomes a button hunter with one more. Every early squash saves you hits later.

items.title: Damage sticks
items.body: Evolving does not fully heal a bug: hits it took before it grew still count. Finish wounded bugs first.

items.title: Triage by colour
items.body: A button fades to mint green on its first bite, turns yellow at 75% health and coral red at 35%. Defend the red buttons first.

items.title: Scroll before you pay
items.body: Scrolling is always free and can outrun the swarm. A Jump costs 50 points and Jump + Zap 200, and every rescue raises both prices by 25.

items.title: Zap only to save a button
items.body: A zap clears a 140–220 px radius but pays 1 point per kill with no combo multiplier, and each zap adds another 150 to its price. Use it when a button is about to fall, not to farm points.

items.title: Shared scoreboard icons
items.body: The scoreboard uses the family's shared action icons for sound, pause, minimize and Recall.

items.title: Keys stay reachable
items.body: Pause, sound and close stay accessible while the scoreboard is minimized.

items.title: Same swarm
items.body: Sounds, palette, engine state and behaviour are unchanged.

items.question: Do I need to install anything to play Swarm Protocol?
items.answer: No. Swarm Protocol plays on this page in your browser. Press Play, and press Escape or Recall when you are done to give the page back.

items.question: Can I play Swarm Protocol on a phone?
items.answer: Yes. Tap a bug to squash it. Phones keep a steady fill and lighter effects.

items.question: What happens to the page when I play?
items.answer: Bugs eat the page's letters into 0 and 1 and drain the colour from its buttons. Recall restores what the game changed and still owns.

items.question: Can I put Swarm Protocol on my own site?
items.answer: Yes. It is open source (MIT), as an npm package or a self-hosted drop-in ZIP. Your visitors never load it from GitHub or a game server.
